lesson_title: The Sweating Can: A Year of Geography in Three Objects
hook_text: A cold cooldrink can, a cracked mud pan and a drought-stricken dam — that's your whole geography year.
clip_script: Fetch a cold cooldrink can from the fridge and set it in the sun. Within a minute the outside is wet. No leak — the air did it. Air always carries invisible water vapour, and when it's chilled against that icy metal it passes its dew point and the vapour condenses into droplets. That can just taught you dew, fog, frost and every cloud in the sky. Now find a dried-out pan after a Karoo summer: the mud has hardened and cracked into stiff plates resting on softer mud beneath. That's the earth itself — rigid plates riding slow currents of hot rock, and everything from the Himalayas to earthquakes comes from those plates pulling apart, pushing together or grinding past each other. Last object: a farm dam falling through a drought. Every old water level leaves a pale ring on the banks — ring below ring. Each ring joins points at exactly the same height. Congratulations: you can now read contour lines — crowded rings mean steep ground, and where they cross a stream, the V points uphill. One can, one mud pan, one thirsty dam — the atmosphere, the restless crust, and mapwork. The whole revision session builds each one into full exam answers, including the gradient routine that ends in 1 in 15.
visual_style: Macro shots: condensation beading on a can, cracked mud polygons from above, drone pull-back over a receding dam with visible waterline rings; quick overlay sketches converting each object into its diagram.
mood: Everyday objects turning into revision gold.
pacing: Three-object structure, one beat each, quick overlay payoffs, confident close.
call_to_action: Watch the full revision session and walk into your final exams calm.
